description.summary: a program's own part of its window's title bar

protocol.description:
Dukovo's window server draws a frame around every window: a title bar with the window's icon, its title and three buttons, and a border. A program that wants a part of the title bar for itself, for tabs or a search box, asks for it with this protocol. The window server keeps the frame, the icon, the buttons and a strip to move the window by; the program draws the rest of the bar.
Whether a program gets the part it asks for is the person's choice, kept by the window server. A program is told which it is with the bar event and draws its window accordingly.

interface.name: dukovo_title_bar_manager_v1

description.summary: gives windows a title bar object

interface.description: The global a program binds to share title bars with the window server.

entry.name: already_exists
entry.summary: the toplevel has a title bar object already

request.name: destroy
request.description: The title bar objects made with the manager stay as they are.

request.name: get_title_bar

description.summary: make the title bar object of a toplevel

request.description:
Makes the title bar object of a toplevel. A toplevel has one at the most: asking for a second while the first is alive is the already_exists error.
The window server answers with a bar event, before the toplevel's next configure event.

interface.name: dukovo_title_bar_v1

description.summary: a toplevel's title bar, shared with its program

interface.description:
While a toplevel has a title bar object, the window server may share the toplevel's title bar with the program. The bar event says whether it does.
When the toplevel is destroyed, the object does nothing more.

enum.name: mode
enum.description:
In the full mode the title bar is the window server's whole, above the toplevel's window geometry. The program draws nothing of it and its region is not used.
In the shared mode the title bar lies over the top rows of the toplevel's window geometry: the geometry is as much higher as the bar is high. The window server draws the bar over those rows and leaves open the program's region, where the program's own pixels show and the program has the pointer.

entry.name: shared
entry.summary: the program draws its region of it

request.name: destroy
request.description: The toplevel has the window server's full title bar again, from the commit that answers the next configure event.

request.name: set_region

description.summary: say which part of the bar the program draws

request.description:
The rectangle of the title bar the program draws, in the coordinates of the toplevel's window geometry. The window server uses of it what lies in the bar's rows below the first and in the columns from the bar event's left to the geometry's width less its right.
A rectangle whose width or height is not more than 0 is no region: the program draws nothing of the bar.
The region is double-buffered state: it takes effect with the next wl_surface.commit of the toplevel's surface.

event.name: bar

description.summary: whose the title bar is, and its sizes

event.description:
Sent once after the object is made and again whenever a value changes, each time before an xdg_surface.configure event of the toplevel. The program draws its window as the event says from the commit that answers that configure event.
The height is that of the title bar. The left and the right are the columns at the two ends of the bar the window server keeps: the icon's at the left, and at the right the buttons' with a strip the window is moved by.
